 It's been a chilly start to the week, but the Carolinas will see things gradually warm-up each day.
 Wednesday looks mostly sunny again with highs a bit milder - reaching the mid to upper 60s by afternoon.
 Forecast - Wednesday 
 It stays dry through mid-week as things look to warm-up back to more seasonal levels by Thursday and Friday, mostly in the upper 60s to lower 70s.
 5 Day High and Low Temps - Grand Strand 
 5 Day High and Low Temps - Inland 
 Then comes the weekend.
 Right now, the forecast is uncertain, but leaning towards clouds and a chance of some rain with a gusty NE breeze for both Saturday and Sunday.
 Weekend forecast 
 If the low does track closer to the coast and rainfall becomes more likely, rainfall amounts could be substantial, perhaps ranging from 1 to 3 inches.
 Wind and temp compare two.png 
 If it stays farther out over the ocean, amounts would be considerably less.
 Model comparisons - Rain this weekend 
 Three out of the four primary models suggest a hit with a decent amount of rain at this time, but things can certainly change as the week goes on.
 Here's a breakdown on those weekend rain chances as well as the timing per each different model:
 Model timelines for potential rain this weekend 
 A good dose of rain would actually be extremely helpful for the current drought situation, which did get worse last Thursday. A brand new update will be issued on Thursday.
 Despite the bad timing, a steady, widespread soaking rain is badly needed, and this weekend might be the best shot in quite some time to see it.
 If not, it's likely another week of barely any rain, and likely a worsening of the drought conditions across the Carolinas.
